subject.title: Tracking: cross-process orphan-sweep TOCTOU in provider Cleanup paths (apple-container / local-container / external)

question: Should these same-user cross-process races be treated as security-boundary violations requiring all three provider guards before resolving the tracker, or as reliability hardening with different release urgency?
rationale: Repository policy trusts processes under the same OS user but also requires exact ownership before destructive provider actions; automation cannot resolve that classification conflict safely.

options.title: Require all three ownership guards
options.body: Treat live-claim deletion as destructive ownership failure and keep the tracker open until apple-container, local-container, and external fixes are reviewed and merged.

options.title: Classify as reliability hardening
options.body: Retain the fixes but remove the security-boundary designation and prioritize them under ordinary concurrency reliability criteria.

recommendation.title: Require all three ownership guards
recommendation.body: Treat live-claim deletion as destructive ownership failure and keep the tracker open until apple-container, local-container, and external fixes are reviewed and merged.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged provider ownership-proof work establishes the closest precedent for deciding this boundary.
